analyst_view.overall: Leverkusen are 5th and host Paderborn, 13th with one loss in five. The news on Leverkusen keeps improving: coach Carles Martinez said on Friday that Maza is available after his ankle problem with Algeria and that everyone in the squad can start, and Bulinews reports Terrier as the only confirmed absence, with Diaby, Kofane, Doue and Eichhorn all possible (Comunio still lists Eichhorn out). The numbers still count Diaby, Tella, Doue and Eichhorn as missing, and the Bundesliga's predicted lineup has both Maza and Diaby starting. Paderborn are without Gayret, with Baack and Scheller doubtful and Pieringer possibly back. Tobias Reichel referees and his near-average record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and take about 3% off Leverkusen for Diaby, who is now in the predicted lineup, while Maza has also been cleared and Kofane and Tella are back, none of which the numbers see. Terrier is still out, so I go 4% higher, to about 2.7 (was +3; Maza's fitness is the change).

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with Leverkusen expected to have most of the ball against a Paderborn back three that sits deep. Returning forwards change who finishes moves more than how often Leverkusen attack down the flanks, so I stay at 11.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with referee Reichel (4.0 a game) adding about 3%. Paderborn's low recent card count is already in the numbers and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots, already lifted slightly for both sides' recent volume. Leverkusen kept shooting a lot (102 in six) even with forwards missing, so the returns of Maza and Diaby mostly help quality, not volume, and I stay at 31.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. With Maza cleared and Diaby, Kofane and Tella back, Leverkusen's finishing options are better than the numbers assume, so I go 3% higher, to about 10.6 (was +2).
